name: js-only-activation

result.pattern: Modal container ships with style="display:none;" and is shown by JS opening the modal
result.rationale: Modal pattern — admin-only. Hidden by default is correct. JS-only activation is the standard modal pattern; no progressive-enhancement loss because the admin tools require JS to function regardless.

result.pattern: <div id="mvs-import-progress"> and <div id="mvs-import-results"> ship with style="display:none;"
result.rationale: These are state regions toggled by the import flow; aria-live="polite" is set so screen readers announce updates when shown. Same modal context — JS required.

result.pattern: <div class="mvs-custom-key-fields" style="display:none;"> revealed when 'use custom key' radio selected
result.rationale: Conditional admin form section; aria-hidden could be added but the pattern is fine for an admin-screen progressive-disclosure. JS required for the radio handler regardless.

result.pattern: populated by user-search XHR
result.rationale: Empty container hidden by default; populated + revealed by JS when a search query runs. Frontend explore filters — JS required to populate the container, so display:none is correct (showing an empty container would be visually confusing).

result.pattern: Display:none rules in Instagram layout CSS
result.rationale: Three `display: none` rules in the Instagram layout stylesheet. Worth inspecting whether any of them gate progressive enhancement (showing content only after JS hydration) — most likely they're dropdown / overflow-menu hiding which is the standard pattern, but un-verified at the time of this scan.

result.pattern: Visibility modifier classes that apply display:none !important within their breakpoint
result.rationale: These are 1.2.0 Phase 3e standard visibility classes — emitted by StandardAttributes::visibility_classes() based on attributes set in the block inspector. Not JS-driven; pure CSS responsive-visibility pattern. Same shape across all 12 Pro blocks. By design.

notes: Sub-check 2.5 — JS-only UI activation pattern audit. Every plugin has SOME of this and not all of it is bad: admin modals (which require JS to do anything useful) and live-update regions (search results, progress bars) are correct uses. The pattern that's actually a smell — a content-bearing element ships hidden and only-JS reveals it, leaving no-JS users stranded — does NOT exist anywhere in Pro. Of the 6 entries: 5 are documented-acceptable, 1 is templates/layouts/instagram/instagram.css needs-review for the 3 display:none rules (low-priority cleanup target for 1.2.1). Phase 3a/3b/3c/3d/3e blocks DO emit visibility-modifier classes (mvs-hide-*) — by design, these are part of the StandardAttributes responsive-visibility schema, applied to the wrapper element so they don't hide JS-required content. No frontend regression.
